answers.explanation: Layer 2 works one hop at a time. Getting a packet end to end, across many links, is the network layer's job.
Layer 3 hands down a packet (datagram); layer 2 wraps it in a frame.
Each link can use its own protocol: WiFi on the first link, Ethernet on the next, fiber after that. The datagram is re-framed at every hop.
A link protocol's format specification includes the rules for finding frame boundaries.
Flow control paces adjacent sending and receiving nodes.
That's the difference from error detection, which can only notice the damage and then drop the frame or ask for a retransmission.
A walkie-talkie is half duplex. A phone call is full duplex.
Wired links have very low error rates, so they leave recovery to higher layers. Wireless links lose frames often enough that they acknowledge and resend at layer 2.
Layer 2 links frames between neighboring hosts on the same segment of the LAN.
